_doc: Settings only the data pipeline reads (Python scripts and workflows); the app never imports this file. See src/cities/README.md.

imdGrid.note: Visakhapatnam grid point inside GVMC on the Gopalapatnam/Simhachalam side (city centre 17.69 N, 83.22 E). The coastal ocean-cell trap is real here: 17.5/83.0, 17.5/83.25 and 17.75/83.5 are NaN in every IMD year 1991-2025, so a seaward point would write zeros. This cell has values in every year 1970-2025. Checked against IMD's Visakhapatnam airport observatory normal, 'Visakhapatnam(AP)', of 1,054.5 mm (Climatological Table 1991-2020, station index 43149): this cell returns 1,053.4 mm over 1991-2020 (-0.1%). IMD's Visakhapatnam observatory (station index 43150) has a 1991-2020 normal of 1,113.1 mm (this cell -5.4%), and the AP planning department's district normal is 1,117.7 mm (cited in CGWB's 2025 aquifer plan; this cell -5.8%).

recent._note: Matches generate_imd_rainfall.py's grid point, not the city centre, for the Kolkata/Pune reason. Also the coastal one: the nearer seaward cells are ocean in IMD's grid.

ingres._note: Visakhapatnam drills to mandal like Pune. Editions start at 2023-2024, the first in which all eleven current units exist; see the notes for the two redraws the earlier editions sit on.

_notes.drill.district: Title case so the IN-GRES GeoServer's parent_name matches too; the assessment API ignores the case of locname.
_notes.drill.availability_key: Andhra Pradesh's totalGWAvailability adds the in-storage resource (Gopalapatnam 2024-2025: 72,849.24 = 383.53 + 72,465.71 ham). CGWB's stage divides by the extractable figure, which is currentAvailabilityForAllPurposes.
_notes.drill.wfs: Unit polygons: AP's mandals live in gec:indgec_mandal_all (the per-state gec:indgec_vers_andhrapradesh layer holds villages only); the 2023 vintage matches the seven-mandal split.
_notes.provenance_note: Per-city text for the envelope note, the block panel's caveat and its availability label, in place of wording written for other cities. build_drilled reads these four keys only where a city sets them.

ingres.provenance_note: Assessment per mandal inside Visakhapatnam district, for the three editions on today's eleven units (2023-2024 to 2025-2026). Drilled below the district because IN-GRES classes Visakhapatnam district safe in all three (43.85% in 2024-2025) while one mandal inside it, Visakhapatnam Rural, was critical in 2024-2025 (95.06%). This is NOT depth-to-water - IN-GRES does not carry it; measured levels are a separate series from APWRIMS and the AP Ground Water Department.
ingres.history_caveat: The editions shown start at 2023-2024, the first in which all eleven current mandals are assessed: until 2022-2023 the city was assessed as one GVMC unit and Bheemunipatnam had other boundaries. The 2025-2026 IN-GRES edition is newer than CGWB's December 2025 report, and its rainfall input repeats 2024-2025.

block_caveats.Visakhapatnam Rural: In 2025-2026 its extractable resource is revised from 225.3 to 437.1 ham, with 223.88 ham of surface-irrigation recharge where 2024-2025 had none, while extraction stays near 210 ham, so the move from 95.06% (critical in CGWB's 2025 report) to 47.87% comes from a revised input, not measured change. IN-GRES assesses this unit over 39.0 km2; the AP Water Resources Department's mandal map gives Visakhapatnam (Rural) 130.9 km2.
block_caveats.Gajuwaka: In 2025-2026 its estimated industrial draft is revised from 5.4 to 97.0 ham and its surface-irrigation recharge is cut from 111.95 to 19.19 ham, which together take it from 60.47% to 89.39% (semi critical); these are revised inputs, not measured change.
block_caveats.Maharanipeta: In 2025-2026 its surface-irrigation recharge is revised from 171.18 to 561.40 ham and its extractable resource from 1,058.35 to 1,411.17 ham, while extraction stays near 720 ham, so the move from 67.26% to 51.34% comes from a revised input, not measured change. IN-GRES assesses this unit over 123.0 km2; the AP Water Resources Department's mandal map gives Maharanipeta 45.7 km2.
block_caveats.Seethammadhara: In 2025-2026 its surface-irrigation recharge is revised from 103.69 to 53.36 ham and its extractable resource from 205.65 to 156.98 ham, while extraction stays near 103 ham, so the move from 49.78% to 66.40% comes from a revised input, not measured change.
block_caveats.Mulagada: Most of the area IN-GRES calls Mulagada lies in the mandal the AP Water Resources Department's map calls Pedagantyada, around Devada and Palavalasa, so the wells here carry that name. CGWB's 2025 aquifer plan for the Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli urban areas gives Pedagantyada 100 km2 and Mulagada 30 km2, against the 98.8 km2 IN-GRES assesses here, so the two names look transposed.
block_caveats.Peddagantyada: IN-GRES assesses this unit over 15.3 km2, a strip around Gollalapalem and Gopalapatnam. The AP Water Resources Department's map puts those wells in Mulagada and Visakhapatnam (Rural) mandals, and CGWB's 2025 aquifer plan gives Pedagantyada 100 km2, so the names of this unit and Mulagada look transposed.

notes: VISAKHAPATNAM RURAL IS THE MANDAL TO WATCH. In 2024-2025, the edition CGWB printed in 'Dynamic Ground Water Resources of Andhra Pradesh State 2025' (December 2025; district table PDF p.95, mandal table pp.108-109), it extracted 214.2 of its 225.3 ham extractable resource, 95.06%, and was the district's only CRITICAL unit, while Visakhapatnam district as a whole stood at 43.85%, which IN-GRES classes safe. This artifact reproduces that edition's eleven mandal figures to one decimal.

2025-2026 IS THE EDITION THE MAP COLOURS, AND IT IS NEWER THAN CGWB'S DECEMBER 2025 REPORT, which carries 2024-2025. It is the newest edition on IN-GRES, and every mandal's rainfall input repeats its 2024-2025 figure. Its surface-irrigation recharge differs from 2024-2025 in every mandal, and four urban mandals move by more than 15 points, all on revised inputs rather than measured change: Visakhapatnam Rural's extractable resource nearly doubles (225.3 to 437.1 ham, with 223.88 ham of surface-irrigation recharge where 2024-2025 had none) while its extraction slips from 214.2 to 209.2 ham, taking it from 95.06% critical to 47.87% safe; Gajuwaka's estimated industrial draft goes from 5.4 to 97.0 ham while its surface-irrigation recharge is cut from 111.95 to 19.19 ham (extractable resource 605.3 to 519.4 ham), taking it from 60.47% to 89.39% and semi critical; Maharanipeta's surface-irrigation recharge rises from 171.18 to 561.40 ham (extractable resource 1,058.35 to 1,411.17 ham), taking it from 67.26% to 51.34%; and Seethammadhara's falls from 103.69 to 53.36 ham (extractable resource 205.65 to 156.98 ham), taking it from 49.78% to 66.40%. Each moved unit's panel carries its own caveat.

EDITIONS START AT 2023-2024, the first with today's eleven units. IN-GRES also publishes 2016-2017, 2019-2020, 2021-2022 and 2022-2023 under the same district id, but on different units: until 2022-2023 the city was assessed as one 'GVMC' unit of 513.8 km2, which became seven urban mandals (430.2 km2 together) in 2023-2024, and Bheemunipatnam was redrawn from 93.8 to 124.2 to 207.9 km2 (Pendurthi and Anandapuram also changed). A series joined across those redraws would show jumps that are boundary changes. For the record, the single GVMC unit stood at 50.84% (2019-2020), 47.70% (2021-2022) and 56.78% (2022-2023), all safe.

ONE DISTRICT ID, TWO DISTRICTS. Andhra Pradesh divided Visakhapatnam district in April 2022 and IN-GRES kept one id across the change: its district rows cover 8,547.7 km2 in 2016-2017 and 11,050.6 km2 in 2019-2020, then 1,001.7 km2 from 2021-2022, the assessed area of the new district (CGWB's 2025 report gives its geographical area as 1,049 km2). The district figure goes from 27.22% to 45.96% across that change, which is the boundary, not the aquifer. No district series is published here, and no district trend should be quoted across 2021.

IN THE CITY, GROUNDWATER IS DRAWN FOR HOMES. In 2024-2025, 1,676.9 of the 1,776.2 ham extracted across the seven urban mandals (94.4%, summed before rounding) was for domestic use, while in Anandapuram, Padmanabham and Pendurthi more than 95% of extraction is irrigation.
No unit in these three editions is categorised on the salinity axis and none carries poor-quality area, so every figure covers the unit's whole assessed area.

THE MAP OUTLINES ARE APPROXIMATE. They are IN-GRES's own unit polygons (GeoServer layer gec:indgec_mandal_all, 2023 vintage, identical to the active 2025 vintage), but their areas do not equal the areas the assessment was computed over: together they cover 973.8 km2 against 1,001.7 km2 assessed, and Pendurthi's polygon is 77.2 km2 against 21.6 km2 assessed. The colours carry each unit's assessed figures; the outlines only place them.

IN-GRES'S URBAN UNITS DO NOT FOLLOW ANDHRA PRADESH'S MANDAL LINES. The unit IN-GRES calls Mulagada (assessed over 98.8 km2) lies mostly inside the mandal that the AP Water Resources Department's own boundary map (APWRIMS GeoServer layer AP_MANDAL_V3) calls Pedagantyada, around Devada and Palavalasa. The unit it calls Peddagantyada (15.3 km2) is a strip around Gollalapalem and Gopalapatnam. CGWB's 2025 aquifer management plan for the Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli urban agglomerations (Table 1.1) gives Pedagantyada 100 km2 and Mulagada 30 km2, so the two names look transposed. The other urban units differ in extent too: IN-GRES assesses Maharanipeta over 123.0 km2 and Visakhapatnam Rural over 39.0 km2, where the AP map has 45.7 and 130.9 km2. Figures are shown under IN-GRES's names. Each well's panel and label on the groundwater map name the AP mandal its coordinates fall in and, where it differs, the IN-GRES unit; the Mulagada and Peddagantyada panels say the names look transposed.

availability_ham IS THE EXTRACTABLE RESOURCE (the API's currentAvailabilityForAllPurposes). For Andhra Pradesh the API's totalGWAvailability adds the in-storage resource below the zone of water-level fluctuation, which is why Gopalapatnam would otherwise read 72,849.2 ham against an extractable 383.5 ham in 2024-2025.

elevationBands._note: Coastal and hilly: the flood story is the narrow strip under 10 m, and the Kailasa/Yarada ridges are one top band. FABDEM land percentiles: p1=3 p5=7 p20=21 p50=48 p80=88 p95=186 p99=318 p100=587

_notes.sea_is_zero: FABDEM stores this sea as exact 0 m, not as masked pixels, so the NODATA sentinel alone would draw the Bay of Bengal as the 0-2 m band.

elevationBands.provenance: FABDEM V1-2 (Hawker et al., University of Bristol; satellite-derived 30 m DEM with buildings and forests removed) via Google Earth Engine, classified into ground-height bands. The sea (FABDEM's exact 0 m) is removed; there is no city-boundary clip, as we have not found published GVMC boundary geometry. Read them as bands, not spot heights.

adjudicated.about:Delhi: A publisher's official name, not another city's data. The flood source line is 'IMD RSMC New Delhi cyclone reports': IMD's Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre for the Bay of Bengal sits in New Delhi and issues the after-event reports the flood page cites.
adjudicated.about:Hyderabad: A publisher's official name, not another city's data. The groundwater source line names IN-GRES's host, 'IIT Hyderabad', beside CGWB and the AP Ground Water and Water Audit Department.
